senses.definition: (countable) The kind, condition, and/or the set of characteristics of something, as opposed to the quantity of something.
examples: The lattice structure of a steel profoundly changes its qualities.

quotes.text: Something about his bearing was uncommitted, as though he were checking not for some bad quality he knew Feldman had, but for some good quality he was afraid he might have.

examples: While being impulsive can be great for artists, it is not a desirable quality for engineers.
Security, stability, and efficiency are good qualities of an operating system.

senses.definition: (uncountable) Good characteristics in particular; level of excellence; freedom of faults and flaws.
examples: This school is well-known for having teachers of high quality.
Quality of life is usually determined by health, education, and income.
He called for China’s cooperation in efforts to improve air quality.

senses.definition: (attributive, occasionally proscribed) Good worth, good make.
examples: For this building project we need to use quality materials that will last for many decades.
That was a quality game by Jim Smith.
We had some quality time yesterday!
A quality system ensures products meet customer requirements.

examples: A peasant is not allowed to fall in love with a lady of quality.
Membership of this golf club is limited to those of quality and wealth.

examples: To identify quality try asking, "what does it feel like?".
